## Working with pipes in {survey} {.bkg-mountains visibility="uncounted"}

:::::{.columns}
::::{.column width=42%}

Magrittr pipe (`%>%`)

- dot notation

```r
design_object %>% 
  svyglm(design = ., y ~ x)
```

::::

::::{.column}
Base R pipe (`|>`)

- placeholder
    
```r
design_object |> 
  svyglm(design = _, y ~ x)
```
- anonymous (lambda) functions

```r
design_object |> 
  (\(.) 
   svyglm(design = ., y ~ x)
  )()
```

::::
:::::

## Accessing ESS data

1. Create a ESS account and get your [user ID](https://ess.sikt.no/en/api){target="_blank"}

2. Open R environ file

```r
usethis::edit_r_environ()
```

3. Add your user ID to R environ

```r
ESS_USERID="12345678-1234-1234-1234-12345678900"
```

4. Restart your R session

5. Load the ESS data into R

```r
url <- glue::glue("https://api.ess.sikt.no/v1/data/dataFile/10.21338/ess11e04_2?userId={Sys.getenv('ESS_USERID')}")

## Replicate weights overview {.smaller .bkg-ship visibility="uncounted"}

Replicate weights are another method to estimate variability. In general, they are constructed by:

1. Divide the sample into subsample replicates that mirror the design of the sample
2. Calculate weights for each replicate using the same procedures for the full-sample weight (i.e., nonresponse and post-stratification)
3. Calculate estimates for each replicate using the same method as the full-sample estimate
4. Calculate the estimated variance, which is proportional to the variance of the replicate estimates

## Common replicate weight methods {.bkg-ship visibility="uncounted"}

- Balanced repeated replication (BRR)
- Fay's BRR
- Jackknife
- Bootstrap
